args.body:
Hi Dora! I just took a look at your personal website (www.dora-website.com) and wanted to share some feedback.

What works:
- It's clean and loads instantly — no clutter, no pop-ups, no autoplay video. That's a real plus.
- Your email is right there, so anyone who wants to reach you can do it in one click.

Where I'd focus next:
- The site is currently a single line of text, so there's not much for a visitor to actually do. Even a few short sections would make it feel like a real site: a short "About Me" intro, a list of your projects or work, and a way to get in touch.
- Consider adding a profile photo and links to your other profiles (LinkedIn, GitHub, portfolio, social media). Right now there's no way to tell what you do or where else to find you.
- Instead of printing your email address as plain text, a contact form or a mailto: link keeps it clickable while looking tidier.
- A page title and a favicon would help with how the site appears in browser tabs and bookmarks.

Overall it's a nice, minimal starting point — the foundation is there, it just needs a bit more content to show people who you are. Happy to share more specific ideas if you tell me what kind of work you want to highlight!

Best,
Emma Johnson

Hi Eve! I had a look at your blog (www.eve-blog.com) and wanted to send you some feedback.

What works:
- The site is fast and distraction-free, which is exactly the right feel for a personal blog.
- Your love of hiking is a great hook — it's a genuine, distinctive topic that people can connect with.

Where I'd focus next:
- Right now the blog is just one line of text, so there are no posts to read yet. Publishing a few entries (even short ones) would give visitors a reason to come back.
- Since hiking is your thing, you could build a niche around it: trail write-ups, gear reviews, route guides, or a "weekend hikes" series. A clear theme tends to help a blog grow faster than general posts.
- Add an archive or a list of posts, plus tags or categories, so readers can browse by topic.
- An "About" page with a photo and a short bio would help readers connect with you, and an RSS feed makes it easy for people to follow along.
- Photos from your hikes would be a huge asset here — a gallery or a featured image per post would make the blog much more engaging.

Overall, a strong concept in a clean package. The main thing missing is content — once there are a few posts and some photos, it should come together nicely.

Best,
Emma Johnson
